title: Global Public Goods R&D Underprovision
bottleneck: Research with diffuse global benefits — tropical disease, climate adaptation, pandemic preparedness — is underfunded because no single nation captures the returns. Market incentives point R&D toward rich-country problems, and international funding mechanisms are small relative to the need. Philanthropic and multilateral funding fills only a fraction of the gap, and priorities shift with donor fashions.
why_it_blocks: Diseases and climate damages concentrated in poor countries get a fraction of the research their burden warrants. The result is a research agenda set by wealthy markets, not by human need.
current_state: CEPI, the Green Climate Fund, and advance market commitments help at the margins; the structural underprovision persists. Binding international research commitments, analogous to climate finance, have never materialized for health R&D.
